references.text: The leaders had previously made a covenant with the Gibeonites and sworn to let them live, which explains why they now had to keep their promise.
Joshua confirms the fate of the Gibeonites as woodcutters and water carriers, a direct fulfillment of the leaders' words.
Joshua makes the Gibeonites woodcutters and water carriers for the congregation and for the altar of the Lord, further defining their role of service.
In Deuteronomy, woodcutters and water carriers are mentioned as the lowest servants in Israel's camp, showing the humiliating position of the Gibeonites.
The Gibeonites are mentioned again during David's time, where they still hold a special status due to the covenant from Joshua's era.
The temple servants (netinim) who returned from exile are believed to include descendants of the Gibeonites who served as woodcutters and water carriers.
